scope.purpose: Assess whether the review is worth reading, reads naturally, and earns its novelty judgements through precise comparisons.
scope.read: All main, synthesis, arithmetic, geometry/operator, combinatorics and contrastive-test TeX sections; full text of the original 25-page PDF including references; comparison register, citation coverage and identity metadata; selected domain evidence records. Re-read the revised TeX after editorial changes and checked the rebuilt PDF's opening and specific corrected passages.
scope.not_performed: No new proof build, full independent checking of release manuscripts, exhaustive priority search, external referee review or final visual-layout inspection.
scope.approved_ai_disclosure: OpenAI Codex agents contributed substantially to source discovery, literature synthesis, and mathematical exposition.

verdict.audience: Research mathematicians and graduate readers seeking a guided map of proposed advances outside their own specialism; some sections still assume substantial technical background.
verdict.original_pdf: A useful, careful review with a distinctive mechanism-level focus, weakened by a catalogue-like rhythm, dense proof roadmaps and repeated methodological framing.
verdict.revised_source: The earlier overview, clearer definitions, shorter method, more specific application comparisons and sharper conclusion materially improve orientation. The source now reads as a solid specialist narrative review. Dense domain paragraphs and limited explanation of the central new constructions still keep it below an authoritative, unusually engaging survey.
verdict.naturalness: Mostly conventional scholarly prose. Some repeated sentence templates and strings of technical nouns feel assembled. This is a stylistic judgement, not an authorship detector or a reason to alter the disclosure.
verdict.research_contribution: Its value is locating candidate decisive steps, preserving important quantifiers, and comparing them with close antecedents. It contributes synthesis and diagnostic examples rather than new proofs or established cross-field transfer theorems.
verdict.publication_recommendation: Suitable for circulation as a comparative narrative review after final build and layout checks. Remaining suggestions are editorial or depth improvements; this audit found no new substantive contradiction in its mathematical claims. External subject-specialist scrutiny would be needed for authoritative assessments of the proposed proofs.

score_interpretation: Scores are editorial judgements within the stated comparative-narrative-review genre, not probabilities that the release claims are correct. Eight means useful and credible specialist reading with remaining improvements; ten would require unusually illuminating exposition, stronger independent insight and authoritative coverage.

scores.reason: The chosen cases concern major barriers and the review points to specific objects that a reader could investigate.
The original table arrived after the case studies and the method occupied much of the opening. The revised overview and shorter method now orient the reader before details.
Less audit vocabulary and fewer formulaic application lists improve flow. Several paragraphs still repeat the same distinction between inherited tools and proposed compatibility.
Jets, common bases, FPRAS, completeness/soundness and complete operator bounds are now introduced. Some machinery-heavy paragraphs remain difficult without specialist context.
Close comparisons, including contemporaneous preprints and their different hypotheses, prevent several easy novelty exaggerations. Coverage is purposefully selected rather than exhaustive.

The review distinguishes a major endpoint from a new method and identifies the extra quantifier or compatibility at issue. A deeper worked account of one claimed bridge would make those judgements more persuasive.
Established results, preprint claims, documented statement scope and executed proof validation are kept distinct. Bibliographic identity alone is not offered as proof of correctness.

Cancellation, different positivity structures and representation changes form a coherent comparison. These are broad familiar mathematical themes; the diagnostic boundaries carry more original value than the theme names.

scores.category: Original contribution of the review itself
scores.reason: The synthesis and worked controls are useful, but no genuinely new cross-domain theorem or demonstrated method transfer is established. This is an assessment of review originality, not of the magnitude of the underlying proposed results.
The revised text gives concrete input-enlargement, exact-law cost and same-enclosure comparisons. It remains a research agenda without measured practical implementation evidence.

scores.category: Overall as a specialist comparative narrative review

findings.title: Reader orientation was delayed
findings.original_evidence: The method preceded the first mathematical case, while the overview table appeared on page 15. Readers had to retain many family identifiers and methodological distinctions without a map.
findings.remedy: Put the overview immediately after the introduction, explain how its columns should be read, and shorten the method before detailed cases.

findings.title: The most unusual proposed mechanisms are usually named rather than demonstrated
findings.original_evidence: The worked examples mostly demonstrate why weaker statements fail. They rarely show even a miniature version of the central proposed construction actually working. The reader learns where novelty would lie more readily than how the unusual mechanism behaves.
findings.remedy: If a further substantive addition is desired, choose one mechanism and give a short schematic calculation with its preserved quantity and parameter cost. For example, explain the shared-prime dependence in a tiny residue model, or give the simplest logarithmic-jet interpolation conditions. State precisely which part of the main lemma this illustrates.
findings.status: optional improvement; not a required correction
findings.reason: A narrative review need not reproduce the new proofs. One worked central mechanism would nevertheless raise its explanatory and originality scores more than extra citation count.

bibliographic_identity.interpretation: Forty DOI-bearing records have a matched status, and two DOI-bearing records use documented primary-source resolutions. The remaining forty records have primary-record ledger status. This is identity evidence, not eighty-two independent theorem validations.
important_distinctions: A DOI identifies a scholarly object; a preprint DOI does not establish journal peer review.
An arXiv or author-hosted primary manuscript can be a valid source without a DOI.
A correct title/author/year match does not show that the cited passage supports the asserted theorem scope.
A supporting theorem does not, by itself, establish that no earlier equivalent mechanism exists.
bibliographic_identity.metadata_cautions: The source-ledger resolutions matter: Demailly's author name is misspelled in the DOI provider's raw metadata, and Braverman's date fields contain a misleading 2008 entry alongside the journal's 2010 print year. The manuscript bibliography uses the correct primary-source identities. Raw automated 'matched' status should not replace those resolutions.

replacement_passages.purpose: Explain the objective before naming machinery; optional rearrangement after the added E paragraph.
replacement_passages.latex: The Gaussian comparison is designed to bound the logarithm of the cone--Laplace product from below. After normalization, the manuscript collects its remaining terms in an error quantity \(\mathcal E\); proving \(\mathcal E\le0\) therefore gives the desired product bound. The difficulty is that the two cone projections produce matrices that need not commute. The proof chooses coordinates and covariance together, then separates the resulting terms by Hermite degree. Classical covariance representations supply part of this analysis \cite[Proposition~2.1]{GOHoudrePrivault2002}; the proposed new step is controlling the noncommuting terms within the same sharp budget. Its auxiliary curve is tuned to make that control hold on every nontrivial real segment.
replacement_passages.qualification: Retains the reviewed proof architecture; no new theorem or independent validation is asserted. Keep exact curve information and equality discussion in the following paragraph.

replacement_passages.purpose: Make noncommutative order and normalization understandable in fewer technical labels.
replacement_passages.latex: Normalize the matrix-valued analytic test \(F\) by \(\sup_{z\in\Omega}\|F(z)\|\le1\), and choose a top singular pair of \(F[A]\). The proof tests the coefficient functional on both \(FG\) and \(GF\): their order matters because the coefficient matrices need not commute. These two tests supply compatible bounds for the diagonal blocks, while a cross estimate supplies the off-diagonal block. Positivity of the resulting \(2\)-by-\(2\) block then forces \(\|F[A]\|\le2\). The proposed advance is the compatibility of these estimates in every coefficient dimension.
replacement_passages.qualification: The actual normalization correction is already present. This is an optional stylistic replacement, not a request to remove the coefficient-weight detail if needed for the target audience.

replacement_passages.target: synthesis.tex, second paragraph of Cancellation before irreversible estimates
replacement_passages.purpose: Replace a general research recommendation with a concrete cross-case comparison.
replacement_passages.latex: The relevant question in both settings is how much error the cancellation can tolerate. In the correlation problem, the comparison must remain effective as the number of prime supplies grows like \(\log\log X\); otherwise its cost can consume the logarithmic saving. In the kinetic problem, the residual force estimate must keep constants uniform over solution prefixes and leave a momentum loss whose reciprocal-scale series diverges. These are different quantitative tests. They show why a cancellation identity is only the beginning of the argument, and where a sharper bound could change the final conclusion.
replacement_passages.qualification: Both comparisons are already developed in the domain sections. This passage makes their relation explicit without claiming a transferable theorem.
